name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
description: Sprawling 240-acre botanical garden established by Hyder Ali, housing a 3,000-species plant collection, a 19th-century glass house, and a historic pond with migratory birds.

name: Cubbon Park
description: Leafy 300-acre urban park established in 1870, crisscrossed by tree-lined avenues flanked by heritage buildings, an aquarium, and a well-equipped childrens park.

name: Bangalore Palace
description: Tudor-style palace built in 1887 inspired by Windsor Castle, featuring turreted towers, fortified walls, elegant arches, and restored royal chambers filled with antiques and paintings.

name: Tipu Sultan Summer Palace
description: Elegant two-storey teakwood palace built in 1791 as summer residence of Tipu Sultan, showcasing intricate carved pillars, exquisite frescoes, and Mysore-style arches.

name: ISKCON Temple Bangalore
description: One of the largest ISKCON temples in the world featuring a grand marble interior, multimedia exhibits on the Bhagavad Gita, a cultural center, and a popular prasadam restaurant.

name: Vidhana Soudha
description: Iconic neo-Dravidian granite secretariat built in 1956 as Karnataka seat of government, best photographed at dusk when its floodlit dome dominates the city skyline.

name: HAL Aerospace Museum
description: India first aerospace museum, displaying over 50 aircraft from Spitfires to modern jets in an outdoor pavilion alongside scale models, engines, and HAL manufacturing history.

name: Bannerghatta National Park
description: Biodiversity hotspot 22 km south of Bangalore with a zoological park, butterfly enclosure, crocodile farm, and glass-cage safari buses through tiger, lion, and bear enclosures.
